Let \(s=(12)\) and put
\[
u=r-r^2.
\]
In characteristic \(3\), one has
\[
u^3=0,\qquad s^2=1,\qquad su=-us,
\]
and
\[
r=1-u-u^2.
\]
Since \(u^2\) is central, commutator with \(r\) has the same rank as commutator with \(u\).

A natural endomorphism of \(F=U^{\oplus 3}\) is exactly a matrix \(P\in M_3(A)\), acting by left multiplication on each module. Thus natural idempotents are precisely idempotents \(P^2=P\) in \(M_3(A)\), and
\[
(C_E)_{X_n}
\]
has rank \(n\) times the rank of left multiplication by \([P,r]\) on \(A^3\).

Let \(J=(u)\subset A\). Then \(A/J\cong k\times k\), with the two idempotent parts denoted \(+\) and \(-\). Reducing \(P\) modulo \(J\) gives a pair of idempotent \(3\times3\) matrices
\[
(P_+,P_-)\in M_3(k)^2.
\]
The commutator rank is controlled first by
\[
d=\operatorname{rank}(P_+-P_-).
\]
The maximum possible rank is \(12\), attained exactly when \(d=3\). Counting such reduced pairs and their radical lifts gives
\[
N^{(1)}=13340\cdot 3^{18}=5168189323260.
\]

The next possible rank is \(10\), occurring when \(d=2\) and the first radical lift contributes a nonzero socle direction. Counting those lifts gives
\[
N^{(2)}=118560\cdot 3^{16}=5103619241760.
\]

Therefore, for every \(n\ge1\),
\[
\boxed{
\left(R_n^{(1)},N_n^{(1)},R_n^{(2)},N_n^{(2)}\right)
=
\left(12n,\;5168189323260,\;10n,\;5103619241760\right).
}
\]
